title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Policy inputs
text:
Policy inputs
The design applies these selected policies without changing them:
Pairing codes are temporary, single-use, bound to the requesting device, rate-limited and safe under concurrent claims; the claiming person must already be authorized for the destination company and branch; a displayed code is not an enduring credential ([security requirements](security-and-i18n.md#pairing-and-device-lifecycle), FR-02).
Pairing, moving, unlinking and resetting devices is company-wide for administrators and limited to authorized source and destination branches for branch managers; operators need an additional grant ([permission matrix](identity-and-access.md#permission-model-and-default-matrix)). Administrator and branch-manager grants count only in strongly authenticated sessions (P12).
Offline authorization expires no later than seven days after its last successful online renewal (AT-15, P22); commercial deadlines may shorten it (PJ-27).
Unlink needs explicit authorized confirmation, server revocation and a distinct pending-erasure state; private content, configuration and credentials are cleared on reconnection; reassignment to another company requires verified cleanup or a controlled reset; revoked access, unreachable device and confirmed erasure stay distinct (P24).
Player identities are separate from human identities and restricted to their own assignment, media and reports. Raw codes, credentials and credential-bearing links never reach logs, errors, screenshots or support bundles. No custom cryptography or token scheme.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Mechanism overview
text:
Mechanism overview
The flow follows the shape of the OAuth 2.0 Device Authorization Grant ([RFC 8628](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8628)): a device without a keyboard shows a short code, and a person who is already signed in elsewhere enters it. Teluni does not route devices through Keycloak, because devices are not human principals and Keycloak holds only human identities (ADR-0024); the API module plays both the authorization-server and resource-server role for devices.
Player                                API (devices module)                    Panel (signed-in person)
  │ generate 256-bit credential C            │                                      │
  │ POST /device-enrollments              │                                      │
  │   { credentialHash: SHA-256(C), report } │                                      │
  │ ◀── { enrollmentId, userCode, expiresAt, pollInterval }                         │
  │ show userCode on screen                  │                                      │
  │                                          │ ◀── POST /companies/{id}/devices  │
  │                                          │      { userCode, name, branch, rotation }
  │                                          │ claim: PENDING → CLAIMED, insert device
  │ POST /device-enrollments/{id}/status  │                                      │
  │   Authorization: Bearer C                │                                      │
  │ ◀── { status: "paired", deviceId }       │                                      │
  │ GET /device/self (Bearer C)  ────────▶│ configuration + authorizedUntil       │

The device generates its own credential and sends only its hash when enrollment starts. The credential itself never leaves the device until it is used, the server never returns a secret, and a lost response at any step is retried without issuing anything new. This is the central choice in [ADR-0027](../adr/0027-propose-device-generated-credentials-and-code-based-enrollment.md).

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Enrollment
text:
Enrollment
**Start.** `POST /device-enrollments` is anonymous. The body carries the credential hash (32 bytes, base64url) and the device report (see [capabilities](#capabilities-and-rotation)). The server creates a `PENDING` enrollment valid for 10 minutes and answers with the enrollment ID, the user code, the expiry and a 5-second polling interval. A hash that already belongs to a device or any enrollment is refused with `ENROLLMENT_REJECTED`, so one credential can never bind two identities.
**User code.** Eight characters from the 20-consonant alphabet `BCDFGHJKLMNPQRSTVWXZ`, shown as `XXXX-XXXX`, as RFC 8628 section 6.1 recommends: about 34.5 bits, no vowels (no accidental words) and no look-alike digits. Entry ignores case, spaces and hyphens. The server stores an HMAC-SHA-256 of the normalized code under a dedicated `RESTRICTED` key ring (key ID stored with the value, newest key first), never the code, so a database copy does not let anyone enumerate live codes offline. A unique index on the HMAC prevents two live enrollments from sharing a code; a collision on insert is retried with a new code.
**Claim.** In the panel, a person enters the code with a name, a destination branch and a rotation. In one transaction the server locks the company row (tenant data design rule 5), rebuilds the actor's access and requires `devices.manage` on the destination branch and an active company and branch, then moves the enrollment from `PENDING` to `CLAIMED` with a conditional update (`WHERE status = 'PENDING' AND expires_at > now()`), inserts the device with the enrollment's credential hash and report, and writes one `device.paired` audit event. Exactly one of two concurrent claims succeeds; the other, an expired code, a used code and an unknown code all answer the same `PAIRING_CODE_INVALID`, so the answer does not reveal which case applied. The rotation must be one the device reported as supported.
**Status.** The device polls `POST /device-enrollments/{id}/status` with `Authorization: Bearer <credential>`; the server checks the credential against the enrollment's hash. Answers are `pending` (with the polling interval), `paired` (with the device ID) or `expired`. Polling faster than the interval answers `RATE_LIMITED` with the interval to use. Pending enrollments expire lazily: reads treat an expired row as expired and a purge deletes `PENDING` rows one day after expiry, and `CLAIMED` rows 30 days after the claim.
**Commercial hook.** The claim transaction is where PJ-27 will add trial, license and quota admission. Until then only company and branch status gate enrollment.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Device credential and authentication
text:
Device credential and authentication
**Credential.** 32 bytes from the platform CSPRNG, generated and kept by the player in Android Keystore-backed storage (D-07, PJ-12). The server stores only its SHA-256 under a unique index; because the credential has 256 bits of entropy, an unkeyed hash is sufficient for lookup and gives nothing usable from a database copy. The credential is `RESTRICTED`: never in logs, telemetry, errors, audit, query strings or the panel.
**Use.** Device operations declare a new operation access kind, `device`, and expect `Authorization: Bearer <credential>` on paths under `/device/`. The devices module resolves the credential to the device on every request, with no cache, so revocation takes effect on the next request. Device routes never accept the human session cookie, and human routes never accept a device credential. The shared runtime gains only the access kind; the devices module owns the lookup.
**States.** An `ACTIVE` device's credential reaches every device operation. A `REVOKED` device's credential reaches only `GET /device/self`, which answers `{ status: "unlinked", clearRequired: true }`, and `POST /device/self/erasure`, which confirms clearing. Any other credential answers `DEVICE_UNAUTHORIZED` with no detail.
**Rotation.** `POST /device/self/credential` replaces the hash with a new device-generated one. The previous hash stays valid until the new credential is first used, so a lost response leaves the device with a working credential. Rotation is in the last delivery increment; it is not required by the first player.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Check-in and the offline authorization deadline
text:
Check-in and the offline authorization deadline
`GET /device/self` returns the device's ID, name, branch name and time zone, rotation, status and `authorizedUntil`. For an active device, `authorizedUntil` is the database clock plus seven days (AT-15), later capped by a commercial deadline under PJ-27. `PUT /device/self/report` updates the reported capabilities. Each successful device request updates `last_seen_at`, written at most once per minute per device so check-ins do not cause a write per request.
In this design `authorizedUntil` is a server statement in an authenticated HTTPS response. Making it tamper-evident on the device (a signed envelope) and enforcing it against a trusted local clock (AT-16) belong to D-04/PJ-11 and D-07/PJ-12. The panel shows "last seen" and, for unreachable devices, the latest deadline the device could hold, so operators never read server intent as device state.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Capabilities and rotation
text:
Capabilities and rotation
The device report is bounded, validated JSON: application version, protocol version, manufacturer and model (each at most 80 characters), Android version, display width and height in pixels (1 to 16384) and the supported rotations. It is stored as reported and labelled "reported by the device" in the panel; it is not a qualified hardware profile (PH-08), and nothing in this design claims support for a device because it reported a capability.
The configured orientation is a rotation of 0, 90, 180 or 270 degrees clockwise: 0 and 180 are horizontal, 90 and 270 vertical (FR-03). A rotation, rather than a horizontal/vertical flag, tells the player which way the screen is physically mounted. Setting a rotation the device did not report as supported answers `ROTATION_UNSUPPORTED`; the panel offers only reported rotations.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Device lifecycle
text:
Device lifecycle
          claim                       unlink                       device confirms clearing
(none) ─────────▶ ACTIVE ───────────────────────────▶ REVOKED, erasure PENDING ───────────▶ REVOKED, erasure CONFIRMED
                  │  rename, set rotation, move           │ record controlled reset (person)
                  │  (same company only)                  └──────────────────────────────▶ REVOKED, erasure RESET_RECORDED

**Rename and rotation.** Need `devices.manage` on the device's branch and the expected version.
**Move.** Changes the branch within the same company. Needs `devices.manage` on both the source and the destination branch, an active destination branch and the expected version. Moving to another company is not an operation: it is an unlink followed by a new enrollment.
**Unlink.** Needs `devices.manage` on the device's branch, the expected version and an explicit confirmation in the panel that names the device. It sets `REVOKED` with erasure `PENDING` in one transaction; from then on the credential reaches only the two operations above. It cannot be undone; the device is paired again with a new enrollment.
**Erasure confirmation.** When an unlinked device reconnects, it learns `clearRequired`, deletes private content, configuration and its credential locally (PJ-12), and only then calls `POST /device/self/erasure` with the credential it is about to discard. The server records `CONFIRMED`, deletes the credential hash and writes `device.erasure_confirmed`. If the response is lost, the device has already cleared and the record stays `PENDING`, shown honestly as unconfirmed, which is the safe direction.
**Controlled reset.** A device that will never reconnect (factory reset, broken, lost) stays `PENDING`. A person with `devices.manage` can record that the device was reset locally; the record says `RESET_RECORDED` with the actor, not `CONFIRMED`, and audit keeps the difference.
**Reassignment.** The server cannot recognize a physical device across identities, so verified cleanup is enforced where it can be: the player starts a new enrollment only from a state with no credential and no private content, and when it still holds a credential it first completes the erasure confirmation above. A new enrollment always creates a new device identity; the old record keeps its own history. The panel lists unlinked devices with their erasure state until the purge below.
Archived branches keep their devices; archiving a branch that still has active devices answers `BRANCH_IN_USE`, through a guard the devices module registers on the organizations access port, so a device is never left in a branch nobody can manage.

heading: Permissions

Permissions
Two capabilities are added to the organizations domain, which owns role presets:

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Abuse limits
text:
Abuse limits
Proposed initial values:
Enrollment start: the existing per-route rate limit plus at most 20 starts per client address per hour, and at most 10,000 pending enrollments platform-wide, after which starts answer `RATE_LIMITED`. A full pending table makes a guessed code at most 10,000 in 2.56 × 10¹⁰ likely to match.
Claim: at most 10 failed claims per person per 15 minutes and 30 per company per 15 minutes, counted in PostgreSQL from failed-claim rows that record only the actor, company and time. Exceeding a limit answers `RATE_LIMITED` without saying which applied. With these limits an attacker with one account needs on the order of years of attempts per expected match against a full pending table. Many accounts or companies created for guessing remain a residual risk that the signup abuse controls (PH-13) must bound; a successful guess pairs a stranger's screen to the attacker's company, which its owner notices because pairing fails on their side, and no tenant data is exposed.
Status polling: once per polling interval per enrollment.
The per-address limit uses the address Fastify reports for the connection, as the identity routes do; behind a reverse proxy it counts the proxy until trusted forwarding is configured for the production deployment. The general request limit of device routes counts each presented credential instead, under a ceiling of 6,000 requests per address per minute, so screens sharing an address do not exhaust it for each other.
These limits stand on their own; commercial device quotas are PJ-27.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Contracts
text:
Contracts
Human operations (session access, CSRF as elsewhere): `GET /companies/{companyId}/devices` (paginated, cursor-bound, filter by branch and status), `GET .../devices/{deviceId}`, `POST .../devices` (claim), `PATCH .../devices/{deviceId}` (name, rotation, expected version), `POST .../devices/{deviceId}/move`, `POST .../devices/{deviceId}/unlink`, `POST .../devices/{deviceId}/reset-record`. Device operations: the enrollment start and status, `GET /device/self`, `PUT /device/self/report`, `POST /device/self/erasure` and, later, `POST /device/self/credential`. All are TypeBox contracts in the OpenAPI document; the web uses the generated SDK. New expected errors: `PAIRING_CODE_INVALID`, `ENROLLMENT_REJECTED`, `ROTATION_UNSUPPORTED`, `DEVICE_UNAUTHORIZED`, `DEVICE_UNLINKED` (a human change of an unlinked device), `DEVICE_ERASURE_NOT_PENDING` (a reset record without pending erasure), `BRANCH_IN_USE` (organizations), plus the existing `RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND`, `RESOURCE_VERSION_CONFLICT`, `RATE_LIMITED` and strong-authentication errors.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Panel
text:
Panel
A **Screens** view per company (pt-BR "Telas") lists devices with name, branch, status, rotation, last seen and erasure state, filtered to what the person may view. **Pair a screen** asks for the code shown on the TV, a name, a branch the person may manage and a rotation, and shows the reported model and resolution after a successful claim. The device page renames, changes rotation, moves (destinations limited to manageable branches), unlinks with a confirmation naming the device, and records a reset for a pending erasure. Conflicts and unknown outcomes reload and explain, as other company pages do. Copy is in `pt-BR` and `en-US`.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Verification
text:
Verification
Domain unit tests: code generation and normalization, rotation and report validation, lifecycle transitions and permission decisions.
Integration tests against PostgreSQL, with two companies and differently scoped branch managers: claim allowed and denied by scope, destination branch outside scope, resource-ID substitution across companies, expired, replayed and unknown codes answering the same error, two concurrent claims of one code with exactly one success, credential reuse refused, rate limits, revoked credentials limited to the two operations, erasure confirmation idempotence, move scope on both branches, version conflicts, audit rows and the structural composite-key suite.
Contract tests for every expected error and the device access kind; no route accepts the wrong credential type.
Browser component tests for the pairing form, the list and the unlink confirmation, and one end-to-end journey that simulates the player over HTTP: start enrollment, pair in the panel, check in, unlink and confirm erasure.
Physical qualification of the Android flow, key storage and clock behavior remains PJ-12, PH-08 and PJ-14.

Implementation status

Browser component tests cover the pages.
Not yet implemented: an API or panel view of device audit events (they are written and kept with the company), any player beyond simulated HTTP clients (PJ-12), signed authorization (PJ-11) and commercial capping (PJ-27).

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Decisions for review
text:
Decisions for review
The owner approved each item as proposed on 2026-10-19 under [PH-22](human-actions.md#ph-22):
**Enrollment mechanism (ADR-0027).** RFC 8628-style flow owned by the API: the device shows a short code and polls; a signed-in person claims the code in the panel. Devices do not use Keycloak.
**Device-generated credential.** The player generates a 256-bit credential and sends only its SHA-256 at enrollment; the server stores only the hash, never issues a secret and accepts it as a bearer token on device routes only, checked on every request.
**User code.** Eight characters from 20 consonants (`XXXX-XXXX`), valid 10 minutes, single use, stored as a keyed HMAC under a new `RESTRICTED` key ring; every failure answers the same error.
**Abuse limits.** 20 enrollment starts per address per hour, 10,000 pending platform-wide, 10 failed claims per person and 30 per company per 15 minutes, polling once per interval.
**Offline deadline.** Check-in reports `authorizedUntil` as server time plus seven days (AT-15); signing and device-side enforcement are left to PJ-11/PJ-12, and commercial capping to PJ-27.
**Rotation and capabilities.** Rotation of 0, 90, 180 or 270 degrees limited to what the device reports; reports are stored as device statements, not qualified support.
**Unlink and reassignment.** Unlink is immediate, irreversible revocation with erasure `PENDING`; the revoked credential can only learn it must clear and confirm clearing; a person may record a controlled reset, shown distinctly from confirmation; another company always pairs a new identity, and the player enrolls only from a cleared state.
**Permissions.** `devices.view` for all roles in their scope; `devices.manage` for administrators company-wide and branch managers on their branches (both branches for a move); operators need a future additional grant.
**Retention (provisional until PH-13).** Unclaimed enrollments deleted one day after expiry, claimed enrollments 30 days after the claim, failed-claim counters after one day; device records and audit are kept with the company; network addresses are never stored.
Approval authorizes implementation of PJ-08 in local and CI environments with simulated players. It does not select hardware (PH-08), implement the Android player (PJ-12) or qualify any physical behavior.

title: Teluni Device Enrollment and Lifecycle Design
heading: Alternatives considered
text:
Alternatives considered
**Server-issued credential returned once on pairing.** Simpler for the device, but the only copy travels in a response that can be lost, which forces either a re-issue path (more secret-bearing responses) or a stuck device. Rejected in favor of the device-generated credential.
**Device key pair with signed requests (for example DPoP, RFC 9449, or mutual TLS).** Stronger against a copied credential because the private key can stay in Android Keystore hardware, but it adds JWT/proof verification or certificate infrastructure on a single-host pilot with no measured threat requiring it. ADR-0027 keeps the bearer credential behind the `device` access kind so a proof-of-possession scheme can replace it later without changing the enrollment flow.
**Keycloak device grant and service accounts.** Reuses an established implementation, but makes every screen a Keycloak client or user, couples player availability to Keycloak and mixes device and human identities, which the policies keep separate.
**Numeric six-digit codes.** Easier to type on a remote but only about 20 bits; with the same limits an attacker would match a pending code orders of magnitude sooner.
**QR code with a link.** Convenient on phones but puts a credential-bearing link on screen and in browser history; it can be added later as another way to enter the same short code.

title: Orion v3.0.0 Upgrade
heading: Integration decisions
text:
Integration decisions
Preserve Teluni's module compositions, workspace home/sign-in routing, company-scoped navigation, localization, session/CSRF boundaries, light/dark themes, Connected Tiles assets, configurations, player, pilot infrastructure and project documentation. Review automatically merged shared files as well as textual conflicts. Database schemas, migrations, metadata, runtime grants and device/API contracts do not need changes for this release.
Adopt the Vite documentation-selection helper, fail-closed import guard and emitted-artifact/browser tests. Retain the project-owned conditional route composition and use `__ORION_INTERNAL_DOCS__` consistently. The portal owns its engineering layout; the product retains its existing sidebar and shell. Default production output excludes internal pages, catalogs, search and downloads. Keep Teluni's additional public-bundle check. The pilot Docker build uses this default product boundary; no internal build flags are added to deployment configuration.
Define the new build constant through the canonical development selection in Teluni's separate Vitest browser configuration, where components import the route composition. This preserves its development-navigation coverage; actual default/internal build tests and E2E cover the distribution boundary. Test assertions and deadlines remain unchanged.
Keep Vitest's diagnostic attachments ignored alongside Playwright reports, so failed browser checks do not add screenshots to the project's tracked source or publication inputs.
Adopt Button, TextField, compatible ErrorNotice, the category/owner/scope metadata model, component source validation, examples and design guidance. Map the new UI hooks to Teluni's existing semantic theme tokens; keep feature behavior and existing ErrorNotice wording, operation mapping and localized reload label. No speculative UI framework or feature-form rewrite is introduced.
Preserve Teluni's Vite 8.3.5 and Vitest 5.0.5; adopt Fastify 5.12.6 and compatible upstream lockfile security corrections. Keep Teluni's workspace package scope, overrides and extra dependencies.
Prune Orion-only reference implementation and history. Regenerate all portal data from resolved Teluni sources, including deletion of stale foundation-only generated pages.
Orion's published ADR-0018 collides with Teluni's accepted tenant-data ADR-0018. Preserve both identifiers and accepted meaning; import Orion's record under [its own namespace](../adr/orion/README.md), changing only relative links. Apply the same metadata and index validation within each namespace, with regression coverage for duplicate IDs and invalid imported records.

heading: Purpose and current state
text:
Purpose and current state
This checklist records Teluni's prerequisites that require a project-owner decision, a human-controlled account action, an unavailable privilege, or securely supplied external configuration. Every contributor or coding agent performing implementation work must maintain it and must never silently skip work because human intervention is needed.
Teluni (https://github.com/GabriellMDias/teluni) was initialized from Orion (https://github.com/GabriellMDias/Orion). Repository settings verified for Orion—Renovate, branch protection, and security controls—do not apply to this repository; the actions below establish them here. Conditional needs such as an identity provider, durable releases, or a deployment environment become new actions when their trigger occurs.

title: Teluni Human Actions
heading: Maintaining this checklist
text:
Maintaining this checklist
The owner authorized the [Orion v3.0.0 upgrade](foundation-upgrade-v3.md) on 2026-10-23, including autonomous migration, validation, commits and pull-request preparation. Implementation and local Linux qualification are complete, including the post-baseline aggregate and player checks. It requires no new product decision, provider credential or production access. Inspect existing decisions, access, tools, configuration, and prior authorization before requesting human intervention. Complete authorized automation and all useful preparation first.
Keep one stable `PH-NN` ID per coherent action; never reuse or renumber IDs. Split broad items into independently verifiable actions as they become concrete, and add newly discovered actions immediately.
Every action retains its ID, checkbox, owner, status, dependency, and evidence. Active or conditional requests also need the exact action, reason, non-secret configuration names, and verification method. Use `pending`, `in progress`, `completed`, `blocked`, or `changed` consistently with the [plan](implementation-plan.md#maintaining-this-plan).
Before asking the user, provide a concrete request: the exact setting or decision, prepared options where appropriate, why automation cannot finish it, affected task IDs, and how completion will be checked.
If an action blocks work now, mark the dependent plan task `blocked`, link this entry, and surface the request to the user. Continue independent authorized work.
Use `[x]` and `completed` only after verification, recording safe evidence and the verification date. If direct verification is unavailable, record the limitation rather than claiming success.
Reopen an action with `[ ]` if later evidence invalidates completion, access expires, or configuration changes, and record why.
A conditional item that becomes unnecessary remains `[ ]` with status `changed`, an explicit reason, and its future trigger or replacement.

heading: Safe configuration handoff
text:
Safe configuration handoff
Record configuration names, required scopes, environment, purpose, non-secret resource identifiers, and secure destination. Never record passwords, tokens, API keys, connection strings containing credentials, private keys, or complete environment dumps here, in the plan, in chat, or in tracked example files.
Name only implemented configuration keys and link the [generated configuration reference](../generated/configuration/api.md); do not invent variable names in advance.
Humans place secrets directly into the selected protected secret store or an explicitly documented ignored local file. Contributors verify presence and authorized behavior without printing secret contents.
Use synthetic local and test data and ephemeral credentials where possible. Production secrets must not be prerequisites for ordinary development or CI.

**Status:** completed. **Owner:** project owner, with engineering/security review.
**Dependency / trigger:** [PJ-30](implementation-plan.md#current-work); blocks the invitation work remaining in PJ-03, which every real onboarding of a second person into a company needs. Real sending to real people additionally remains gated by [PH-17](#ph-17) and [PH-13](#ph-13).
**Request and reason:** Read the [invitation and email delivery design](invitation-delivery-design.md) and the proposed [ADR-0026](../adr/0026-propose-a-postgresql-outbox-and-smtp-relay-for-transactional-email.md), then approve, reject or adjust each of the design's [ten decisions for review](invitation-delivery-design.md#decisions-for-review): (1) a PostgreSQL outbox written in the producer's transaction, an in-process dispatcher and a provider-neutral SMTP relay through `nodemailer`, with no broker, worker service, provider API or webhooks; (2) at-least-once delivery with up to eight attempts over about 22 hours and failures shown to the inviter; (3) a 256-bit credential stored as a hash, an encrypted delivery copy erased at the message's final state, and the link credential in the URL fragment; (4) acceptance only by a session whose verified email equals the recipient, with no email lookup at invitation time and, until signup exists, only existing verified accounts; (5) active members gain the invited grant, suspended members are refused, removed people return as a new membership (membership uniqueness then excludes removed rows); (6) revalidation at acceptance with no silent narrowing, so a responsibility transfer invalidates the former responsible administrator's pending administrator invitations; (7) who may invite whom, grant expiry, one pending invitation per address and resend replacing it; (8) limits of 50 invitations per company per day, 100 pending per company and 3 emails per address per day, with fixed `pt-BR`/`en-US` templates and no free text; (9) provisional retention of 30 days for message rows and 90 days for invitation addresses after final state, never storing addresses in audit; (10) Keycloak keeps sending its own mail synchronously through the same relay. These are security, privacy and delivery choices with long-lived consequences that the repository requires the owner, not an agent, to approve.
**Configuration:** none. The design names configuration concepts only (relay host/port/TLS mode/username, a `RESTRICTED` relay password, sender address/name and a `RESTRICTED` outbound-mail key ring); settings are added to the canonical configuration schema when implemented. No real relay credentials are needed for local or CI work, which uses Mailpit.
**Verification:** Record the owner's dated explicit decision per item (chat or pull-request review). On approval, mark the design approved and ADR-0026 accepted, complete PJ-30 and resume the PJ-03 invitation increments. A rejected or changed item updates the design and, where it changes the delivery mechanism, ADR-0026 or a new ADR.
**Evidence / blocker:** 2026-10-18: the owner asked for this design for approval; the design and ADR-0026 were drafted and linked from the plan, the product architecture and the decision index. The same day the owner explicitly approved all ten decisions as proposed, including ADR-0026, in chat, and asked to proceed to implementing invitations. It does not choose the real provider or sender (PH-17), set legal retention (PH-13) or authorize sending to real people.

Keep it with two offline backups, and record only the certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint in the player's installation guide. Losing the key means every screen must be reset and reinstalled.
**Configuration:** the release build will read the keystore path, alias and passwords from Gradle properties or environment variables that the player README names when release signing is implemented; never commit their values.
**Verification:** The fingerprint is recorded, an APK signed by the release process verifies with `apksigner verify --print-certs` against it, and an update signed with the same key installs over the previous release on a test device.

New action template
Allocate a new stable `PH-NN`; do not reuse existing IDs. Link it from the blocked or conditional plan task.
## PH-NN

- [ ] **Concrete human action.**

**Status:** pending. **Owner:** actual person or responsible role.
**Dependency / trigger:** Linked task; whether it blocks current work.
**Request and reason:** Exact need, completed preparation, and why authorized automation cannot finish it.
**Configuration:** Exact non-secret names, minimum scopes and secure destination; never secret values. Use "none" if no configuration is needed.
**Verification:** Observable checks required before completion.
**Evidence / blocker:** Dated safe evidence, outstanding limit, or changed applicability.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Access Policies
heading: Status and ownership
text:
Status and ownership
**Decided product policies, 2026-10-18:** the owner answered all 38 PH-11 questions directly. This document owns human enrollment, authentication assurance, recovery, sessions, permission allocation and support policy. The inherited [authentication](../security/authentication.md) and [authorization](../security/authorization.md) controls still govern. [Release policies](release-policies.md) own publication/playback behavior; this policy constrains who can trigger it.
**Accepted provider direction:** self-hosted Keycloak, with the [pinned-source compatibility assessment](identity-provider-evaluation.md#pinned-source-assessment) and owner acceptance recorded on 2026-10-18. Actual deployment remains subject to PH-10 host feasibility and PJ-24 integration qualification. No recurring identity/email procurement budget is authorized. This does not establish zero operating cost or an available email service. Google is the only selected external login provider; Microsoft is not part of this delivery.
**Accepted architecture:** the owner explicitly approved [ADR-0024](../adr/0024-propose-keycloak-and-server-managed-human-sessions.md) and [ADR-0025](../adr/0025-propose-application-owned-scoped-access-profiles.md) on 2026-10-18. They do not supersede accepted ADR-0012. **Implemented:** Keycloak login, server-managed sessions, OTP step-up and the first organization/access increment; [D-02 status](identity-session-design.md#implementation-status) and [D-01 status](tenant-data-design.md#implementation-status) own the implementation evidence and remaining workflows. PH-11 is completed for selection, and PH-20 records owner approval and the PJ-03/PJ-24 implementation request. External provisioning and unperformed release qualification remain pending.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Access Policies
heading: Enrollment and account continuity
text:
Enrollment and account continuity
Support **public registration with automatic company activation** after verification and abuse checks, rather than requiring routine Teluni approval. The new company is separate from every existing company; matching a name, claimed business identifier or email domain never proves control of an existing tenant. Activation does not imply a free plan, trial duration, paid entitlement or unlimited resources. Completed PH-12 [commercial-policy selection](commercial-policies.md#pilot-and-public-trial) defines the bounded trial. Actual offer/capacity/coverage evidence remains PH-18, billing readiness PH-19 and notices PH-13 before public activation or applicable paid operation. A pending prerequisite must not silently turn the selected product into invitation-only onboarding.
Offer email/password and optional passkeys through the established identity provider, plus optional Google login. Do not make an external social account the sole administrative recovery method. Localized enrollment/login/recovery must support `pt-BR` and `en-US`.
Require trusted email verification before company access. Company invitations are recipient-bound, single-use, revocable and valid for **seven days**; a resend invalidates the previous pending invitation. Acceptance requires the matching authenticated identity and explicit membership confirmation. Changing recipient requires a new invitation. Verification establishes mailbox control, not legal identity or company ownership.
Link login methods only through an explicit flow proving the existing account and new method with recent authentication. Never merge accounts solely by equal email. A new email must be verified, the previous address notified and the stable application identity preserved. Method removal must leave a usable method meeting assurance requirements. This applies equally to first Google login and later linking.
One human identity may hold independent memberships in multiple companies and different scopes/roles within each. Switching company explicitly revalidates access. A company administrator cannot enumerate the person's other companies or manage their global credentials.
Each company has a **designated responsible administrator** who approves additional company administrators. Other administrators retain the matrix's ordinary administrative capabilities but cannot bypass that approval. Establish the first responsible administrator from the verified automatic signup flow; controlled assisted enrollment may serve support/migration needs without overriding the public-registration decision. Responsibility transfer requires an attributable, strongly authenticated flow and successor acceptance; prevent loss of the last active administrator or responsibility without a valid transfer. Responsibility is a company relationship, not an inferred legal-ownership determination or platform privilege.
Provision platform administrators through a controlled procedure, outside public signup and tenant administration. Use individual administrative accounts distinct from ordinary customer operation, with phishing-resistant assurance and prepared recovery. Product administration does not grant access to provider administration, infrastructure, database credentials or customer content.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Access Policies
heading: Assurance, recovery and abuse
text:
Assurance, recovery and abuse
Strong authentication is mandatory for platform administrators, company administrators and branch managers. Operators may opt in, and companies can require it for everyone. Any operator/profile granted publication or automatic-price distribution must also meet the strong-authentication requirement. Do not let custom role labels bypass an assurance requirement attached to a capability.
Prefer passkeys with user verification; password plus an authenticator-app second factor is the selected alternative, with protected single-use recovery codes. Platform administration requires a phishing-resistant method and protected recovery. Social login or a generic passkey label does not alone prove equivalent assurance: qualify the actual flow and assertion. Email-only recovery cannot bypass mandatory MFA. Do not use SMS as the default method.
Require strong authentication no more than **five minutes** old when promoting administrators, changing credentials/MFA/email, transferring responsibility, granting support access, exporting in bulk or unlinking/destroying in bulk. Ordinary authorized publication/price operations use the normal compliant session, without a new prompt for every save. Sensitive operations by users without an enrolled adequate factor must first obtain the required assurance. Confirmation dialogs do not constitute authentication.
Use provider-owned password recovery with enumeration-safe public responses. The selected reset-link target is **15 minutes**, single-purpose and single-use; verify exact invalidation semantics in the selected version. Successful password recovery revokes earlier sessions. MFA recovery first uses a valid alternate authenticator or recovery code. Suspected compromise offers global session termination and a support channel.
Complete loss of recovery methods uses exceptional assisted recovery with proportionate evidence, waiting/notification to previous channels, review and audit. The operational procedure, waiting interval, evidence criteria and escalation remain to be reviewed before use; no instant-unlock promise is made. Seek independent review for higher-risk cases when available, without claiming a two-person control in a one-person operation. Insufficient evidence denies access. Do not introduce personal security questions, agent-created temporary passwords or email-only removal of MFA. Company administrators may repair local membership but cannot reset another person's global identity. Prepare a separate accountable recovery path for the sole platform administrator/last responsible company administrator.
Apply context/operation rate limits, progressive delays, enumeration-safe responses and monitoring, without permanent attacker-triggered lockout. Additional challenges need demonstrated need, accessibility/privacy review and cost approval; they are not a default on every interaction. Numerical anti-abuse limits and provider password-policy parameters require technical review rather than invented vendor defaults. No external challenge subscription is authorized.

text:

Five minutes, with independent session/account/membership enforcement

List sessions using minimized, justified metadata; allow termination of one or all. Background polling/refresh does not count as human activity and cannot extend absolute duration. Warn before timeout and protect recoverable drafts without leaking them across account/company changes or retaining protected caches after logout. Detailed concurrent-session accounting across provider and application sessions remains design/qualification work.
**Accepted browser architecture, implemented by the identity module:** server-managed application sessions with an opaque protected browser cookie; provider access/refresh tokens remain server-side. Compose this capability into the modular backend where appropriate rather than adding a microservice by default. Use established OIDC Authorization Code with PKCE and established session/security components; do not invent token issuance, crypto or password handling. Evaluate `Secure`, `HttpOnly`, `SameSite`, narrow cookie scope, explicit CSRF protection, state/nonce/redirect validation, fixation prevention, refresh rotation/replay/concurrency, logout propagation and token minimization. [D-02](identity-session-design.md#implementation-status) records the concrete controls and remaining qualification; the API contracts and configuration schema own route/cookie/configuration facts.
The internal API bearer boundary remains ADR-0012. A browser cookie must terminate at a reviewed session boundary that obtains the legitimate issuer access token; it is not a second implicit credential accepted by every domain route. The current verifier returns principal ID/scopes, not session or assurance evidence; extend integration contracts deliberately through technical review rather than trusting browser-supplied session IDs, role flags, timestamps or MFA claims.
Validate current application account/session/membership state in addition to JWT signature/expiry to meet the 30-second bound. Cache invalidation, session linkage and sensitive-write race handling need explicit implementation evidence. A valid five-minute JWT alone cannot satisfy that bound. Provider logout and application logout must be reconciled, including reuse/replay and local/global termination. Human logout does not revoke unrelated company memberships or player identities.
On provider, email or session infrastructure failure, unavailable flows report a safe temporary failure. Existing operations continue only while trusted identity, validity and authorization can still be established; otherwise deny protected operations and preserve recoverable work safely. A key/session-store outage is not permission to skip checks. There is no offline administrative panel or public emergency credential. Players retain their independently selected bounded offline policy, not these human-session limits.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Access Policies
heading: Permission model and default matrix
text:
Permission model and default matrix
Support readable default roles plus company-customized profiles built from explicit business capabilities and scopes. The application owns memberships, profiles and resource authorization, not arbitrary provider groups or self-editable identity attributes. Check company, branch, resource, operation, assurance and current state on the server, including background jobs and generated data. This is a product policy; the accepted technical direction is ADR-0025; its concrete mechanism and verification remain implementation work.
Grants combine within their explicit scopes. A person can manage one branch and observe another. A suspended account/membership or expired grant always denies; no grant means deny. Newly created branches do not silently enter a restricted branch grant. Company-wide administrative scope is an explicit grant. Avoid arbitrary negative-rule languages, cyclic inheritance or an unrestricted role shortcut. Grantors cannot confer authority they lack; company grants never confer platform authority. Profile edits must show affected users/scopes and be audited.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Access Policies
heading: Publication impact and delayed work
text:
Publication impact and delayed work
An authorized designated price save triggers automatic publication under PH-09. Before accepting it, authorize the mutation **and all affected published targets**. If any target is outside scope, **reject the entire price mutation** with a safe explanation. Do not partially distribute it, modify the company base price anyway or create an out-of-scope approval request as an automatic fallback. An explicit authorized branch override may be used only when the model and local impact permit it. A permitted shared edit cannot grant hidden publication power.
Authorized publishers normally publish directly. A company may optionally require independent approval by branch/operation; default is disabled, with no self-approval where required. For covered prices, entering a proposal is not saving an effective price: the authorized approval commits that price and triggers automatic publication. This explicit policy qualifies the PH-09 save behavior without turning ordinary drafts into live content. P27 still requires denying an out-of-scope price mutation; optional approvals do not provide a bypass. Approval-chain configuration must identify eligible reviewers, prevent scope escalation and clearly distinguish proposed, approved, saved, queued and active states. No approval module is implemented or inherited from Orion's removed reference feature.
Revalidate company/actor/target authority before an outstanding intent effects a protected change/publication. If authority has been removed/reduced, block the not-yet-effected intent and require new attributable authorization, retaining original authorship. A valid version already authorized and issued continues its normal delivery lifecycle; removing its author does not automatically cancel company programming. Incident response may revoke specific publications/identities. Revalidation cannot silently expand old targets or allow stale work to overwrite newer generations.
Company administrators remove only the local membership; other memberships and global identity remain. Departure does not delete company content. Global disablement is an identity operation. Company suspension denies new protected server operations, with explicit reconciliation for already-authorized offline players; [Commercial policies](commercial-policies.md#payment-expiry-cancellation-and-retention) own commercial/cancellation consequences and distinguish limited commercial access from security suspension; PH-18/PH-19 retain real offer/billing readiness. Historical attribution remains meaningful subject to PH-13 retention/deletion rules. Never promise instantaneous erasure of unreachable devices.

title: Teluni Human Identity and Access Policies
heading: Support, audit and continuity
text:
Support, audit and continuity
The [commercial support policy](commercial-policies.md#hardware-onboarding-and-support) owns coverage/service boundaries; actual coverage remains unverified under PH-18. Routine customer-content support requires an explicit company-administrator grant: reason, scope, maximum default duration **one hour**, read-only default and separate write authority. Support uses its own identity, with visible/audited activity; **no impersonation in this delivery**. Platform operations may manage customer lifecycle metadata without implicit content browsing. A support grant never authorizes provider/database/infrastructure access.
Emergency access requires a distinct exceptional procedure with justification, strong authentication, scope, expiry, audit and notification afterward where applicable. It creates no permanent secret user, universal password or unrestricted standing customer-content access. Evidence criteria, available reviewers and execution/revocation steps must be reviewed before use, honestly reflecting team size. A routine support grant is not emergency authority.
Users can review their sessions and receive relevant credential/recovery notices. Company administrators see company-scoped audit; branch managers see only their branch operations. The platform receives minimized events needed for security/operation. Audit invites, grants/profile changes, assurance/recovery/revocation, support, prices/publications and relevant failures with actor/scope/action/outcome, excluding secrets and full payloads. Security-audit retention and metadata such as IP remain PH-13; the PH-09 operational-report retention is not a legal/security retention decision.
Require application-stable principal IDs, application-owned memberships/permissions, isolated environments and synthetic test identities. Back up/restore identity state under PH-10 and reconcile revocations after restoration. Portability is required, but P37=A does **not** require a pre-pilot export/import proof as a separate acceptance gate; qualify migration when selected/needed and document available mechanisms/limits. A migration may require safe password reset or authenticator reenrollment; do not promise export of every factor or session. No production credentials in CI or cross-environment token acceptance.
